The negative part of X + Y is also controlled by |X| plus |Y|.

This result does not require independence.

It does not require a finite state space.
It does require that the random variables be defined on a common probability space.
If they are not on the same space the expression X + Y is not defined without first choosing a joint model.
Once a common space is chosen the same integrability argument applies.
The finite expectations therefore prevent the expectation of the sum from being undefined or infinite.
